name: Application-Specific Pipelines
text:
# Application-Specific Pipelines


## Overview
Application-Specific Pipelines are specialized [training and optimization](#6838-coarse-to-fine-sparse-volume-training.md) procedures tailored to distinct downstream tasks, diverging from the [standard NeRF](#979-nerf-volumetric-rendering-coarse-fine-sampling.md) reconstruction loop to address specific constraints such as monocular pose estimation or text-guided scene editing. Unlike the general [NeRF Training Loop](970-nerf-training-loop.md) which optimizes a single radiance field for novel view synthesis, these pipelines decouple or augment the optimization objectives to handle tasks like 6-DoF camera pose recovery in Plenoxels environments or compositional object insertion into existing [NeRF](#1185-nerf-neural-radiance-fields.md) scenes.

## Shared principles
The children of this family share the principle of task-specific objective functions and data structures that extend beyond standard RGB [photometric loss](#9563-photometric-loss-rawnerf-variant.md). They utilize pre-trained scene representations as a fixed or partially fixed background, optimizing only specific parameters (camera poses or local object fields) rather than the entire scene. They often employ numerical gradient approximations or [compositional rendering](#11182-compositional-rendering.md) formulations to handle tasks where analytical derivatives are unavailable or insufficient for the specific application constraints.

## Subtopics

### [DPPE (Dense Pose Estimation in a Plenoxels Environment)](9640-dppe-dense-pose-estimation-in-a-plenoxels-environment.md)
[DPPE](#9640-dppe-dense-pose-estimation-in-a-plenoxels-environment.md) is a 6-DoF monocular RGB-only pose estimation procedure for Plenoxels environments that recovers the ground truth camera pose after a perturbation by minimizing errors in re-rendering using stochastic gradient descent and numerical gradient approximation. It sets itself apart from analytical derivative-based methods (like Teigen et al. [30]) by using numerical central differencing, making it generalizable to any scene representation where re-renderings are not prohibitively expensive, and from iNeRF by leveraging Plenoxels' speed to render the full image at each step rather than subsampled rays.

### [GO-NeRF](11181-go-nerf.md)
[GO-NeRF](#11181-go-nerf.md) is a pipeline for generating text-prompt-controlled 3D virtual objects at user-specified locations within an existing 3D environment represented as a NeRF, while preserving unchanged scene content. It sets itself apart from [standard NeRF training](#985-nerf-training-loop-with-random-ray-batching.md) by decoupling the object generation from the scene representation, using a compositional rendering formulation with 3D-aware opacity maps to handle occlusions and prevent unintended modifications to the original scene. Unlike methods that retrain the entire scene, GO-NeRF optimizes a new NeRF representation only within a user-defined 3D bounding box.

### Dynamically-informed iNeRF Estimator
A state estimation method that uses an iNeRF initialized with a dynamics prior, optimized only via photometric loss, acting as a recursive Bayesian filter with infinite state covariance [S1]. The process loss is set to 0 [S1]. An iNeRF estimator initialized without a dynamics prior will very quickly diverge [S1].

## Background
The concept of application-specific pipelines in [radiance field optimization](#44-radiance-field-optimization.md) emerged as NeRF and its variants were applied to robotics and interactive editing. DPPE was developed to enable vision-only robot navigation in neural radiance worlds, specifically addressing the need for robust pose estimation in Plenoxels environments [S1]. GO-NeRF was introduced to facilitate text-guided 3D editing, allowing users to insert objects into existing scenes without retraining the entire field [S1]. The dynamically-informed iNeRF estimator was proposed as a baseline for robot state estimation in NeRF environments, highlighting the instability of standard iNeRF estimators without dynamics priors [S1].
